title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 135
paragraphs: It is established as a sign of manly excellence, next after excellence in fighting, to be able to show many sons; and to the men who have most, the king sends gifts every year, for they consider number to be a source of strength. They educate their children, from the age of five to twenty, in three things only: riding, shooting with the bow, and speaking the truth. But before the boy is five years old, he does not come into the presence of his father, but lives with the women. This is done for the following reason: if the child should die while he is being brought up, he may not be the cause of any grief to his father.
